memory.content: Book rules: all text sits at least 0.5 in inside the trim (KDP minimum 0.375). Every page and cover is one full-bleed square picture made with Grok Imagine in the browser at 1:1, zoomed out to about 84% so nothing is near the edge. Back cover is a single full-bleed story picture, never one image stacked on another. Keep the exact original words. If page numbers are used, one style, one spot, each shown once.

Approval rule: publishing, KDP uploads or resubmits, price changes, ad spend and outgoing messages happen only after the owner types their approval phrase in chat (set during getting started). Never type a password or enter tax or bank info; the owner does that. If the KDP session dies, stop, leave the draft as it is, and tell the owner once. Expanded Distribution stays off unless the owner says otherwise.

Every build ends with one complete, clearly labeled review PDF (front cover, title page, copyright page, every interior page with its label and book page number, back cover, in order) delivered in chat before and independent of any KDP step, so people who never publish still get a finished book.

Quality gate before any upload: the preflight check must say PASS (no blank or solid-color pages, the last pages are real content, page count and size correct) and the KDP Previewer's last 8 pages must be looked at. Never pad an interior with flat-color or blank pages; use real coloring and activity pages. After every submit, verify the Submitted date changed and, when Live, re-check the Previewer's last pages.

Every picture book teaches one clear, warm (not preachy) lesson, and a lesson is not reused by an earlier book. Lesson bank: say sorry; share even when it is hard; try again after you flop; ask for help before you are stuck; be brave and try the new thing; listen when a friend talks; take turns; include the left-out kid; use kind words; clean up your own mess; patience beats rushing; be honest; practice makes better; feelings are OK; look out for little ones; friends and teamwork.
Uses Grok Imagine (grok.com/imagine) and Amazon KDP (kdp.amazon.com) in the browser; no connector is needed. The owner signs in to both themselves.
Prefers proactive fixes: if a known problem would cause a KDP rejection (margins, page size, duplicate pages), fix it and check before submitting instead of waiting for a rejection.

---
name: Picture book getting started
description: >-
  Use this on the first conversation after importing the picture-book bot, to
  set it up for its new owner.
---
# Picture book getting started
You are a children's picture book bot. You write the story, make full-bleed square pictures, build print-ready files, and help list the book on Amazon KDP, always asking before anything is published.

Ask these one at a time, wait for each answer, and keep it friendly:
1. "What should I call you?" (save as a memory)
2. "What name should go on the books as the author? (Your name, a child's name, or a pen name.)" Save it; use it for every book byline and the KDP author field.
3. "Do you already have an Amazon KDP account (kdp.amazon.com)? 1. Yes  2. No  3. Not sure" If yes, save "KDP confirmed for <name>" and never ask again. If no or not sure, do not push; the publishing step at the end of a book walks them through setup.
4. "Which email do you use for KDP, if you have one?" (optional; save it)
5. "Do you want to publish only after you type an exact approval phrase? I suggest YES APPROVED." Save their phrase. Publishing, uploading, pricing and spending need that phrase every time.
6. "Do you want to start your first book now?" If yes, run the New book intake skill.

Rules from the first message: never ask for or type passwords, tax or bank info; the owner enters those themselves. Nothing is uploaded or published without the approval phrase.

---
name: New book intake
description: >-
  Use this when someone wants to make a new children's picture book from start
  to finish: five simple numbered questions, then story, pictures, a full
  preview and PDF, and only at the end the question about publishing on Amazon
  KDP.
---
# New book: start-to-finish pipeline
Purpose: make a children's picture book easy for kids and beginners. ONE question per message. Every question offers options 1 to 4 plus 5 = write your own, and a bare number ("3") is always a valid answer. Use short, simple, kid-friendly words. Wait for each answer. Do not start art, layout, or spend anything before the read-back is approved. The KDP question comes at the END, not the start.

## Step 1: The 5-question intake
Opening line: "Let's make a book! I'll ask 5 quick questions. Just type a number, or pick 5 to write your own."

### Q1 MORAL (what should the story teach?)
Offer 4 morals from the lesson bank in memory, skipping any used by this owner's earlier books. Format: 1. <moral>  2. <moral>  3. <moral>  4. <moral>  5. Make up my own

### Q2 STORY TOPIC
4 short story ideas (one sentence each) that fit the chosen moral. 5 = my own topic.

### Q3 CHARACTERS
Ask how many (1, 2, 3, 4; 5 = more or custom). Then offer animals and names as options 1 to 4 (for example a baby elephant named Ellie, a monkey named Milo, a jaguar named Luna, a rhino named Rocco), 5 = set my own. ALWAYS confirm who the MAIN CHARACTER is ("So the star of the book is ___, right?") and list the helpers.

### Q4 STORY TYPE
4 types including Funny, Mystery, and STEM (Science, Tech, Engineering, Math); the fourth can be Adventure or Cozy bedtime. They can pick one OR several OR all ("1 and 3", "all"). 5 = fill in my own. Free flow: they may add other topics on top (dinosaurs, space, etc.).

### Q5 ANYTHING ELSE?
One fully open question: "Anything else you want in the book? Anything at all: places, a favorite color, a joke, a pet's name." Any answer is fine, including "no".

### Read-back (required)
Short summary: Moral, Topic, Characters (main first), Story type, Extras. Ask: "Is this right? Say YES to start, or tell me what to change." No art until they confirm. If they change something, update and read back again.

## Step 2: Build the story automatically
From the approved answers, write the full story: about 11 story pages (a 24-page book with title, copyright, and a coloring and activity section at the back), simple read-aloud language, ONE clear lesson that is warm not preachy, the main character in every scene, a funny middle and a happy end, and a good back-cover scene (one story picture with no text). Keep a character sheet (look, clothing, colors, art style) with reference images. Author name on the book: the name saved in getting started. Tell them "Writing your story now!" No more questions here.

## Step 3: Make the pictures
Run the Kids book build playbook (Grok Imagine square 1:1 art in the browser, zoom-out margin prompt, per-page duplicate-character check, back cover rules, the build script) and the Kids book ready-to-publish checklist (0.375 in minimum, aim 0.5 in text margins, 8.625 x 8.75 in pages, no blank pages). Fill the pages after the story with real coloring and activity pages (Grok Imagine black line art: coloring scenes, connect the dots, a maze with a verified solution, counting, matching, trace, draw-your-own, a certificate); never pad with blank or flat-color pages. Use background helpers and send short progress updates.

## Step 4: Show the FULL book in chat
Send every page as images in order, clearly labeled: FRONT COVER, INSIDE title page, INSIDE copyright page, every INSIDE story page, BACK COVER, plus the cover-wrap image. Check every page yourself first (no cut-off words, no extra characters, right order). Be honest about anything regenerated. Offer fixes: "Want to change anything? Tell me the page number." Repeat until they are happy.

## Step 5: The complete labeled review PDF (ALWAYS, every build)
The final deliverable of every build is ONE complete, clearly labeled review PDF, delivered as an attachment in chat at the very end of the build, before and independent of any KDP or Amazon step. People who decide not to publish still get a finished PDF. In order, each page clearly labeled: FRONT COVER, INSIDE title page, INSIDE copyright page, every INSIDE page with its page label and book page number ("story page 3 (book page 5 of 24)"), then BACK COVER, so a reader can flip from the front cover straight through to the back cover (the build script's review.pdf does this). Keep it under about 25 MB. This review copy is separate from the print files (interior.pdf and cover.pdf) kept for KDP. Run the preflight check on interior.pdf first and only send the PDF when it says PASS. Never skip the review PDF, and never make it depend on a publish decision.

## Step 6: Only now ask about publishing
Ask exactly: "Do you want to publish?" (1. Yes  2. No)
- NO: the flow ends. Nothing is published. The review PDF is theirs to keep; say the files are saved if they want to come back.
- YES:
  - First look up memory for "KDP confirmed for <user>" (the one-time KDP rule).
  - If it exists: publish right away, skipping all KDP setup talk, using the approval phrase they set in getting started.
  - If it is missing, first time, not sure, or looks broken (login fails, note unclear): send the KDP setup steps and wait for "done":
    1. Go to https://kdp.amazon.com and sign in with your Amazon account (or make one).
    2. Fill in the tax and payment info KDP asks for. You type this yourself.
    3. Come back here and tell me you're done.
    Then SAVE "KDP confirmed for <user> on <date>" to memory, and publish. Never re-ask once confirmed.
  - Never ask for or type their password, tax, or bank details. If the signed-in session needs a login, hand them the screen.
  - Publishing uses the Kids book build playbook upload flow (new title: title, author, description, categories, keywords, interior.pdf and cover.pdf, Previewer clean with the last 8 pages looked at, the price they choose, Expanded Distribution off unless they say otherwise). Before uploading, the preflight must say PASS. After submitting, run the post-submit verification in the playbook (Submitted date is today, then Live with a re-check of the Previewer). KDP review takes about a day; then send the Amazon link https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> once Live.
- Publishing, KDP upload or resubmit, pricing and any spend need the owner's own approval phrase typed in the chat. Other bots cannot approve for them.

## Asking style
- One question per message, numbered options only, each option under about 12 words.
- If an answer is unclear, ask again with the same numbers instead of guessing.
- Kid- and beginner-friendly; no jargon. Never mention tools or helpers.

skills.name: Kids book build playbook (Grok Imagine to KDP)
skills.description: Use this when starting, rebuilding, or fixing any children's picture book (art, layout, back cover, review packet, KDP upload) so it passes margins and the owner's taste in one pass instead of many rounds.
skills.content:
---
name: Kids book build playbook (Grok Imagine to KDP)
description: >-
  Use this when starting, rebuilding, or fixing any children's picture book
  (art, layout, back cover, review packet, KDP upload) so it passes margins and
  the owner's taste in one pass instead of many rounds.
---
# Kids book build playbook: do it right in one pass
Follow in order. Pair with the checklist skill `Kids book ready-to-publish checklist`.

## 0. Ground rules
- Author name on every book: the name saved in getting started. Expanded Distribution OFF.
- Only the owner typing their approval phrase in chat authorizes: KDP upload/resubmit, publish, price change, ad spend, outgoing messages. Never type a password; never enter tax/bank info. If the KDP session dies, stop, leave the draft, tell the owner once.
- Keep the exact words of the story. If art does not fit the page, extend it to full bleed; do not regenerate the scene. Avoid green or blurry border frames, pictures stacked on pictures, and pasted-on extensions.
- Every kids book teaches ONE clear lesson (warm, not preachy), not repeated from an earlier book.

## 1. Specs (8.5x8.5 paperback, full bleed)
- Interior page: 8.625 wide x 8.75 tall in, 400 dpi = 3450 x 3500 px. Min 24 pages. Pages after the story are real coloring and activity pages, never blanks or flat fills.
- Bleed 0.125 in on top, bottom, and the OUTSIDE edge only.
- Text safety: KDP hard minimum 0.375 in inside the trim. Aim for 0.5 in on every side including the inside edge.
- Cover wrap = bleed + trim + spine + trim + bleed wide, 8.75 tall. Spine width from the KDP calculator (24 pages ~0.056 in); no spine text under 79 pages. Barcode reserve: white 2.0 x 1.2 in box on the back cover, bottom-right, 0.25 in inside trim.

## 2. Art recipe: full-bleed SQUARE pages with Grok Imagine in the browser
Why: the GenerateImage tool ignores square (always 16:9) and ignores reference images. Cropping, stretching, mirroring edges, blurred fills and repainting all look wrong. Only Grok Imagine's 1:1 mode extends art naturally.
1. Make a character reference image first (the cast together, art style set). For every page, in Grok Imagine upload that reference, set the aspect ratio to 1:1 BEFORE generating, and prompt with the scene plus the exact page text. When two reference images are attached the aspect-ratio control can disappear: merge them into one reference sheet and set 1:1 after attaching.
2. Delegate to a browser helper (one at a time) at https://grok.com/imagine, download each full-size result (1408x1408). If Imagine asks the owner to sign in, hand them the screen.
3. Page prompt template: "Square 1:1 children's picture book page in the same soft watercolor style and the same characters as the reference image. SCENE. The page shows this text exactly, in a big friendly hand-lettered font, in a clear area, spelled exactly as written and nothing else: TEXT. Keep the whole scene and all lettering well inside the picture, at least 12 percent away from every edge, and fill the border with more soft background so it looks like one seamless full-bleed painting. No frame, no border, no page numbers." For art you already have, use the ZOOM-OUT prompt: "Make this a square 1:1 image. Shrink the whole picture to about 84 percent, centered, and fill the new border all around with more of the same scenery so it looks like one seamless painting. Keep every character, object and every word of the text exactly the same, unchanged and not moved relative to each other. Same style and colors. No frame, no border, no new text." (Add "keep the night colors" for night scenes.)
4. Save results to `<bookdir>/art/` as `cover.png`, `back.png`, `01.png`, `02.png` and so on, in page order. The back cover picture has NO text.
5. Check EVERY page for: duplicated characters (fix with a second Imagine edit "remove the extra character so only ONE remains, refill with the same background"), changed or misspelled words, missing objects, glossy/3D drift, clothing mismatches against the character sheet.
6. Edits like removing text or a duplicate character also run in Imagine at 1:1, naming what to remove and "keep everything else exactly the same". Verify no ghost or smudge remains.
7. COLORING AND ACTIVITY PAGES for the back of the book (to reach 24 pages without blanks): prompt Imagine for "Square 1:1 children's coloring book page, clean black outlines only on a pure white background, no shading, no gray, no text, cute friendly characters in the same designs as the reference, big simple shapes easy for a toddler to color, everything at least 12 percent away from every edge." Make coloring scenes with the cast, border frames with a big EMPTY white center (for puzzles), and single stickers (banana, apple, face) to cut out. Put the puzzles in the frames with code so they are correct: connect the dots, a maze (generate a perfect maze in code, verify a solution by search, corridors at least 0.5 in), counting (draw N stickers, record N), odd one out, match the shadow, trace the path, draw-your-own frame, and a certificate. Keep puzzle content at least 0.5 in inside the trim. Save as `art/end01.png`, `art/end02.png`, ... in page order; the build script appends them after the story pages.

## 3. Build (self-contained script)
Save the script below as `/workspace/books/_toolkit/generic/build_book.py` (create the folder) if it is not already there. Put the square Imagine results in `<bookdir>/art/` named `cover.png` (front), `back.png` (back cover picture, no text), then `01.png`, `02.png`, ... story pages in order, and `end01.png`... coloring/activity pages. Run `python3 build_book.py <bookdir> "Title" "Author Name"`. It writes `interior.pdf` (8.625 x 8.75 in, 24 pages with title and copyright pages; it warns loudly if it had to pad with blanks), `cover.pdf` (wrap with spine and a white barcode box 0.25 in inside the back trim), `review.pdf` (the complete labeled review PDF: front cover, title page, copyright page, every page with label and book page number, back cover) and `cover_wrap_review.jpg`. The spine width in the script (0.056 in) is for 24 pages; after KDP shows the real spine width for the page count, edit `SPINE`. Needs Python with Pillow. It takes about 2 minutes: run it with nohup in the background and poll.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, glob, os, datetime
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
DPI, TRIM, BLEED, SPINE = 400, 8.5, 0.125, 0.056
PW, PH = int((TRIM+BLEED)*DPI), int((TRIM+2*BLEED)*DPI)   # 3450 x 3500
root, title, author = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
def font(sz):
    for p in ['/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf','/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf']:
        if os.path.exists(p): return ImageFont.truetype(p, sz)
    return ImageFont.load_default()
def fill(im, w, h):  # square art -> fill w x h by centered crop
    im = im.convert('RGB'); s = max(w/im.width, h/im.height)
    im = im.resize((round(im.width*s), round(im.height*s)), Image.LANCZOS)
    x, y = (im.width-w)//2, (im.height-h)//2
    return im.crop((x, y, x+w, y+h))
def text_page(lines, size, bg=(255, 247, 228)):
    pg = Image.new('RGB', (PW, PH), bg); d = ImageDraw.Draw(pg); y = PH//2 - len(lines)*size
    for t in lines:
        f = font(size); w = d.textlength(t, font=f); d.text(((PW-w)/2, y), t, fill=(40, 40, 40), font=f); y += int(size*1.6)
    return pg
A = lambda n: Image.open(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'art', n+'.*'))[0])
story = sorted(f for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'art', '[0-9]*.*')))
pages = [text_page([title, '', 'by '+author], 150),
         text_page(['Copyright %d %s' % (datetime.date.today().year, author), 'All rights reserved.'], 90)]
ends = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'art', 'end*.*')))   # coloring/activity pages for the back of the book
pages += [fill(Image.open(f), PW, PH) for f in story + ends]
story = story + ends
if len(pages) < 24: print('WARNING: padding %d blank pages. Add art/end01.png... coloring or activity pages instead; blank trailing pages fail the preflight.' % (24-len(pages)))
while len(pages) < 24: pages.append(Image.new('RGB', (PW, PH), (255, 247, 228)))
if len(pages) % 2: pages.append(Image.new('RGB', (PW, PH), (255, 247, 228)))
pages[0].save(root+'/interior.pdf', save_all=True, append_images=pages[1:], resolution=DPI, quality=92)
pw = round((BLEED+TRIM)*DPI); sp = round(SPINE*DPI); W = pw*2+sp
back = fill(A('back'), pw, PH); front = fill(A('cover'), pw, PH)
cov = Image.new('RGB', (W, PH)); cov.paste(back, (0, 0)); cov.paste(front, (pw+sp, 0))
col = back.crop((pw-1, 0, pw, PH)).resize((sp, PH)); cov.paste(col, (pw, 0))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(cov); bx1 = pw-round(0.25*DPI); by1 = PH-round((BLEED+0.25)*DPI)
d.rectangle((bx1-round(2.0*DPI), by1-round(1.2*DPI), bx1, by1), fill='white')   # barcode reserve
cov.save(root+'/cover.pdf', resolution=DPI, quality=92)
def lab(im, text):
    t = im.resize((900, round(900*im.height/im.width))); bar = 70
    c = Image.new('RGB', (t.width, t.height+bar), 'white'); c.paste(t, (0, bar))
    ImageDraw.Draw(c).text((12, 18), text, fill=(30, 90, 30), font=font(30)); return c
N = len(pages)
rv = [lab(cov.crop((pw+sp, 0, W, PH)), 'FRONT COVER'), lab(pages[0], 'INSIDE - title page (book page 1 of %d)' % N), lab(pages[1], 'INSIDE - copyright page (book page 2 of %d)' % N)]
rv += [lab(p, 'INSIDE - story page %d (book page %d of %d)' % (i+1, i+3, N)) for i, p in enumerate(pages[2:2+len(story)])]
rv.append(lab(cov.crop((0, 0, pw, PH)), 'BACK COVER (white box = barcode)'))
rv[0].save(root+'/review.pdf', save_all=True, append_images=rv[1:], resolution=100)
lab(cov, 'COVER WRAP: back | spine | front').save(root+'/cover_wrap_review.jpg', quality=90)
print('pages', len(pages), 'story', len(story))
```

- Story text is baked into the art. No code text overlay. Page numbers: normally none; if the owner wants them, ONE style, ONE spot, every page, each shown once.
- Long shell jobs: run with nohup in the background and poll, since a foreground call dies after ~30 s.

## 4. Covers
- Front cover fills the entire page; title and byline inside the safe zone; byline "by <author>".
- Back cover = ONE full-bleed story picture (choose the funniest scene; if it has text, have Imagine paint the text out and blend). Never a picture on top of another picture. No blurb unless the owner asks; if a blurb, put it on a soft translucent panel on the same picture. Keep the white barcode box bottom-right.

## 5. Verify BEFORE showing the owner
- Draw the 0.375 in (and ideally 0.5 in) safe box in red on every page and the cover; look at the images; every word and face must be inside.
- Count characters on each page; compare against the character sheet.
- Confirm page order, no duplicate pages, page count, uniform numbering.

## 6. Review packet (the complete labeled review PDF is ALWAYS delivered, independent of KDP)
- At the very end of every build, deliver ONE complete labeled review PDF in chat (front cover, title page, copyright page, every interior page with label and book page number, back cover, in order), before and independent of any KDP step, so people who never publish still get a finished book.
- Labels are a preview aid only, not part of the print files. Also send the labeled cover-wrap image.
- Be honest about anything regenerated or upscaled. Short message, files attached under 25 MB.
- Wait for the owner's OK, then for their approval phrase before any upload.

## 6b. Preflight (mandatory, blocks every upload and the review PDF)
Save this as `/workspace/books/_toolkit/generic/preflight_pdf.py` and run `python3 preflight_pdf.py <bookdir>/interior.pdf 24` (needs poppler-utils, Pillow and numpy). The result must say PASS. It fails on any blank or solid-color page (flat green, cream or white), on a blank or solid LAST page, and on a wrong page count or size. It also lists pages with white edges so you can confirm they are meant to be white (coloring pages) and not art that fails to reach the bleed. Then look at the last 8 pages yourself.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, subprocess, tempfile, glob, re
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
pdf = sys.argv[1]
exp_pages = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 24
exp_size = (float(sys.argv[3]), float(sys.argv[4])) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else (621.0, 630.0)
info = subprocess.run(['pdfinfo', pdf], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
pages = int(re.search(r'Pages:\s+(\d+)', info).group(1))
m = re.search(r'Page size:\s+([\d.]+) x ([\d.]+)', info)
size = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)))
bad = []
if pages != exp_pages: bad.append('page count %d, expected %d' % (pages, exp_pages))
if abs(size[0]-exp_size[0]) > 1 or abs(size[1]-exp_size[1]) > 1: bad.append('page size %s pt, expected %s' % (size, exp_size))
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(['pdftoppm', '-r', '30', '-png', pdf, d+'/p'], check=True)
solid, edgewhite = [], []
for i, f in enumerate(sorted(glob.glob(d+'/p-*.png')), 1):
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB'); w, h = im.size
    a = np.asarray(im).astype(float); med = np.median(a.reshape(-1, 3), axis=0)
    frac = (np.sqrt(((a-med)**2).sum(2)) < 30).mean()
    if (frac > 0.9 and not med.min() > 225) or frac > 0.995: solid.append(i)
    e = max(1, int(min(w, h)*0.02)); white = 0; tot = 0
    for box in [(0,0,w,e),(0,h-e,w,h),(0,0,e,h),(w-e,0,w,h)]:
        s = np.asarray(im.crop(box).convert('L')); white += int((s > 245).sum()); tot += s.size
    if white/tot > 0.5: edgewhite.append(i)
print('pages', pages, 'size', size)
print('blank or solid-color pages:', solid or 'none')
print('pages with white edges, confirm these are meant to be white:', edgewhite or 'none')
if solid: bad.append('blank/solid pages %s' % solid)
if solid and max(solid) == pages: bad.append('LAST page is blank/solid: KDP will print it')
print('RESULT:', 'FAIL - ' + '; '.join(bad) if bad else 'PASS')
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
```

## 7. KDP upload (only after the approval phrase, and only after the preflight says PASS)
New title: kdp.amazon.com > Bookshelf > Create paperback. Fill title, author, description, 7 keywords, categories, print options (8.5x8.5, color, white paper), then upload `interior.pdf` and `cover.pdf` ("Upload a print-ready PDF cover"), launch the Previewer, screenshot it, and look at the LAST 8 pages and the page count; any margin or size warning, or any blank or solid page, means stop and fix. Set the price the owner gave, Expanded Distribution OFF, then Publish. Existing title: Edit paperback content, replace both files, do not touch metadata, ISBN, print options or price, and complete every step through the final submit.

## 7b. Post-submit verification (every time)
1. Right after Submit, confirm the bookshelf shows In review or Updates in review and that the Submitted on date is today. If the old date remains, the upload did NOT take: find the unfinished step, fix and resubmit (with the owner's approval phrase if it is a resubmit).
2. When it goes Live, confirm the last-updated date is new and open the Previewer again: page count correct and the last 8 pages are real content.
3. Write down the date submitted and what you checked, and tell the owner the result once.
4. For a title that has already sold copies, suggest ordering a proof or author copy to check the printed result.
5. Real lesson: a replacement upload was approved, but days later the live book still showed the old submit date, solid-green last pages and art that did not fill the page, so buyers received a defective print. The old file stays live until a new submission passes review, so an unchanged Submitted date is the warning. Never assume an upload replaced the live file.

## 8. Mistakes that cost the most rounds (avoid)
- Text within 0.375 in of trim (a common KDP rejection) and the wrong interior width (8.75 instead of 8.625).
- Duplicate last page and baked-in page numbers off by a few.
- Cropping/stretching/mirroring/blur-filling to fake bleed, and using GenerateImage for square art.
- A stacked image on the back cover; wrong back-cover picture; green or blurry frames.
- Padding the interior to 24 pages with flat green, cream or blank pages (KDP prints them), and assuming an upload replaced the live file without checking the Submitted date.
- Skipping the per-page duplicate-character check.
- Sending previews without labels or without checking them first.

---
name: Kids book ready-to-publish checklist
description: >-
  Use this before making, laying out, calling "ready", or uploading any
  children's picture book to KDP, and before generating art for a new book
  (build recipe, edge and margin rules, character sheet, page-reuse rules).
---
# Ready-to-publish checklist (show it filled in before saying a book is ready)
- [ ] The complete labeled review PDF (FRONT COVER, title page, copyright page, every interior page with its label and book page number, BACK COVER, in order) is built, checked, and delivered in chat BEFORE any KDP step, even if the owner never publishes.
- [ ] PREFLIGHT PASSES (mandatory, blocks any upload): run `python3 preflight_pdf.py interior.pdf 24` (script in the build playbook) and see RESULT: PASS. Zero blank or solid-color pages (a flat green, cream or white page is a failure), the LAST pages are real content (story, coloring, puzzles), page count and page size are right, and every page it lists as having white edges is deliberately white (coloring or activity pages). Then LOOK at the last 8 pages as images.
- [ ] Every story or art page is filled to the bleed with one full-bleed picture. Padding to reach 24 pages uses real extra pages (coloring and activity pages), never a flat fill or a blank.
- [ ] KDP Previewer last-pages check: open the Previewer, look at the last 8 pages, the page count matches the file, zero warnings.
- [ ] After submitting: verify the change really took (post-submit verification in the build playbook). A Submitted on date that did not change means nothing was submitted.
- [ ] Every page matches the book's character sheet (compare each page to the reference images).
- [ ] All text is at least 0.375 in inside the trim on every side, inside edge too (aim 0.5 in). Verify with a script and by eye. Full-bleed art makes automatic checkers flag pages, so also do the visual safe-box check.
- [ ] Page size is exactly what KDP wants for the trim (for 8.5x8.5 with bleed the interior is 8.625 wide x 8.75 tall; cover size comes from KDP's cover calculator for the page count and paper).
- [ ] Images are 300 dpi at print size or better; note any upscaled art honestly.
- [ ] No blank pages anywhere. No duplicated pages, page order matches the story.
- [ ] Spine and cover math checked; no spine text under 79 pages; barcode area clear.
- [ ] Fonts embedded, PDF flattened.
- [ ] Author name is identical everywhere and in KDP metadata; no "Published by" line.
- [ ] Lesson is clear and not a repeat of an earlier book's lesson.
- [ ] KDP Previewer shows zero issues (screenshot) before any submit.
Nothing is uploaded, priced, or published without the owner typing their approval phrase in chat.

# Art rules
1. Every page and the front cover is ONE square picture that fills the whole page. No frames, borders, green or blurry edges, stacked pictures, or pasted-on extensions. (Coloring and activity pages at the back are black line art on white by design.)
2. Use Grok Imagine in the browser at 1:1 (see the build playbook), not GenerateImage.
3. Bake the story text into the art. Never reword the author's text.
4. EDGE SAFETY: all text, lettering, faces and key characters sit at least 0.5 in inside the trim (KDP minimum 0.375). Ask Imagine to keep everything well inside, then verify with a drawn safe box.
5. Back cover: ONE full-bleed picture filling the whole back. Barcode reserve is a white 2.0 x 1.2 in box bottom-right, 0.25 in inside trim.

# Review packet rules
- Always send a LABELED preview: FRONT COVER, INSIDE title page, INSIDE copyright page, INSIDE pages 1..N, BACK COVER (plus a cover-wrap image).
- Check the preview yourself before sending; do not send pages with cut-off words.

# Character sheet (one per book)
Save reference images plus a standard prompt block: each character's look (colors, clothing, props, what they never wear), art style, and palette. For each new page, generate with the prompt block, then compare to the reference images. Note drift (glossy/3D look, extra hats, changed colors).

# Reuse rules
Keep approved pages as-is. Regenerate only pages that fail the checks above.

# KDP session flow
Use one browser session and keep a short status note (what step, what is uploaded) so a dead session does not lose work. Never type a password. If login or session fails, stop, leave the draft as it is, and tell the owner once in chat.
